# Central Asia B2G Intelligence

> Open research on B2G AI and digital-government opportunities in Uzbekistan + Kyrgyzstan. Typed knowledge graph mapping decrees, institutions, decision-makers, donor programmes, and global precedents to deployable initiatives. Apache 2.0.

## Pillar pages

- [Page not found](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/) — The link you followed does not match any page in the Central Asia B2G Intelligence research site. The site is organised around six pillar pages plus the methodology, lenses, scoring rubric, and an honesty page that names what we did not find.
- [Donor programme pipeline](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/donors/) — This pipeline lists 49 active and forthcoming donor programmes from World Bank, ADB, EU, EBRD, UN agencies, and bilaterals that fund AI and digital government work in Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. Every record names the donor's TTL or project manager and the government counterpart they work with.
- [Central Asia B2G Intelligence](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/) — This open research catalogues 100 deployable AI and digital-government initiatives across Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, scored on five axes and grounded in 100 decrees, 105 institutions, 117 decision-makers, 49 donor programmes, and 100 global precedents. Every claim is typed, verifiable, and cross-referenced. 28 initiatives are rated Tier-A — deal-ready.
- [Initiative top 100](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/initiatives/) — This is the headline list: 100 deployable AI and digital government initiatives across Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, scored on five axes and tier-bucketed. 28 initiatives are Tier-A — every key reference field is verified, and a credible 12-month deal path is documented. The scoring rubric is on the Scoring page.
- [Decision-makers and diaspora bridges](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/people/) — This list catalogues 117 named decision-makers across Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan with mandate over AI or digital procurement, plus 16 diaspora advisors who shape policy from London, Dubai, Moscow, San Francisco, and other cities. Only Tier-1 and Tier-2 individuals are shown publicly; outreach scripts and warm-intro paths stay in the private vault.
- [Live procurement](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/procurement/) — This page tracks 50 live and forthcoming AI or digital government tenders in Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, including donor-funded procurement through World Bank STEP and ADB CSRN. Each tender is annotated with incumbent risk, win probability, and the authorising decree where traceable.

## Data pages

- [Decree atlas — Kyrgyzstan](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/decrees/kg/) — This atlas catalogues 44 presidential decrees, government resolutions, and sectoral laws shaping AI and digital government in Kyrgyzstan, with 7 currently in their six-to-eighteen-month active implementation window. Every decree is verified on the official government source and cross-checked in independent media.
- [Decree atlas — Uzbekistan](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/decrees/uz/) — This atlas catalogues 56 presidential decrees, government resolutions, and sectoral laws shaping AI and digital government in Uzbekistan, with 11 currently in their six-to-eighteen-month active implementation window. Every decree is verified on the official government source and cross-checked in independent media.
- [Institution map](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/institutions/) — This map covers 105 state institutions across Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan with AI or digital mandate, organised in eight tiers from Presidential Administration through Cabinet, line ministries, agencies, SOEs, regulators, working groups, and donor PIUs. Every institution names its current head, parent, and recent decisions.
- [Solopreneur MVPs (UZ + KG)](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/mvp/) — This is a parallel track to the institutional B2G initiatives: 200 solopreneur-bootstrappable MVPs grounded in the knowledge graph and HubSpot's $1M Solopreneur MVR framework. 51 are Tier-A. Every idea has a one-week build plan, a quantified validation target, and a price point grounded in local purchasing power.
- [Solopreneur MVPs — Kyrgyzstan](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/mvp/kg/) — This is a parallel track to the institutional B2G initiatives: 100 solopreneur-bootstrappable MVPs grounded in the knowledge graph and HubSpot's $1M Solopreneur MVR framework. 25 are Tier-A. Every idea has a one-week build plan, a quantified validation target, and a price point grounded in local purchasing power.
- [Solopreneur MVPs — Uzbekistan](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/mvp/uz/) — This is a parallel track to the institutional B2G initiatives: 100 solopreneur-bootstrappable MVPs grounded in the knowledge graph and HubSpot's $1M Solopreneur MVR framework. 26 are Tier-A. Every idea has a one-week build plan, a quantified validation target, and a price point grounded in local purchasing power.
- [Sectoral trends](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/trends/) — Twelve sectoral trends shape the AI and digital government opportunity surface in Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan in 2025–2026: public administration, justice, health, education, agriculture and water, energy, transport, finance, security, environment, tourism, and labour migration. Each trend is grounded in specific decrees, donor programmes, and named decision-makers.

## Methodology

- [The six analytical lenses](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/lenses/) — Six lenses cut across every record in this research: the Karimov-to-Mirziyoyev Inversion in Uzbekistan, the Japarov Concentration in Kyrgyzstan, the Decree Half-Life that opens six-to-eighteen month implementation windows, Donor Co-Financing behind sixty to ninety percent of digital budgets, the Diaspora Bridge of senior advisors, and the Russian/CIS Substitution Window opened by post-2022 vendor retreat.
- [Methodology](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/methodology/) — A seven-wave multi-agent pipeline turns Russian, Uzbek, and Kyrgyz primary sources into a typed knowledge graph. Eleven specialised agents work in three parallel research waves, one synthesis wave, one adversarial audit, and one outreach wave. Cross-model verification on a strict twenty-dollar OpenRouter budget keeps every Tier-A claim independently re-checked.
- [Scoring rubric](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/scoring/) — Every initiative is scored on five weighted axes: Speed-to-Contract (25%), Strategic Moat (20%), Defensibility (20%), Capital Access (20%), and Russian/CIS Fit (15%). A weighted total of 7.5 or more puts an initiative in Tier-A — deal-ready with every reference field verified. Below 6.0 is Tier-C or worse.

## Optional

- [Honesty: what we did not find](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/honesty/) — This page documents the limits of this research: known gaps, dead-end research pathways, opaque domains, and contradictions we could not resolve. Honesty is a first-class output here. A research artifact that hides what it does not know is not trustworthy.
- [Provenance and audit trail](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/provenance/) — Every record in this research carries one or more cited sources, totalling roughly 402 references across decrees, institutions, people, and donor programmes. Every cross-model verification call to OpenRouter — Perplexity Sonar Deep Research, Sonar Pro, o4-mini-deep-research, Owl Alpha, and Gemma — is logged as an evidence card under state/external/ in the public repo.

- [About this research and its author](https://avaluev.github.io/ca-b2g-research/about/) — Alexandr Valuev built this research as an open, reproducible alternative to the Big-4 frontier-market opportunity reports that cost six figures and disappear into a PDF. Every prompt, every script, every quality gate is public. Every claim is typed. Every error is named.
